Subject: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility & deployment options (MedWise)

Hi John — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary from call:
- MedWise use case: patient-facing summarization + clinician notes ingestion; some prompts will contain PHI.
- Key ask: whether Redwood can sign a BAA and which deployment mode(s) allow processing of PHI.
- Compliance artifacts requested: SOC 2 report, security questionnaire, architecture notes for PHI boundaries.

What Redwood can provide / clarifications:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report (security & availability controls). I attached a short security overview PDF and our standard vendor questionnaire to kick off your team’s process.
- BAA: We can execute a BAA, but PHI processing is only supported on Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment modes. Our hosted multi-tenant API cannot be used for PHI.
- PHI boundaries: For Dedicated and Private we provide: encryption in transit & at rest, access controls, audit logs, and options for customer-managed KMS (Private). We recommend limiting PHI-containing inputs to pinned model endpoints with dedicated capacity and enabling KV/prefix caching restrictions.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please share your security questionnaire (I attached our template to help map controls).
2) If you want a technical deep-dive, Rishi (copied) can run a short call to walk deployment architecture and data flow.
3) Legal Ops — if you can confirm your timeline for a BAA review, we’ll prioritize internal sign-off and get you our standard BAA template.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf, Vendor_Sec_Questionnaire_MedWise.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll sync with Rishi and Avery on timing.

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility & deployment options (MedWise)

John — thanks for the quick questions and the partial questionnaire. Short answers below; Rishi included more technical detail in a follow-up email.

- Dedicated: yes — Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool that we allocate to a single customer. There is no mixing of customer model inference traffic or persistent KV caches across tenants. Metadata and logs are logically separated; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. We can provide a more formal separation diagram for legal/security.
- Private (VPC): Private gives you a customer-controlled network and (optionally) customer-managed keys. Redwood’s control plane can be configured to operate over a private connection; we do not retain access to your customer-managed KMS keys when that option is chosen. Audit logs and access controls remain available; we can remove any telemetry collection per contract if required.
- BAA: I’m attaching our standard BAA template and will loop legal internally. We can target your 4-week timeline — please confirm once you’ve fed the questionnaire back to us.

Next steps: I’ll set up a 30m technical session with Rishi next week to walk through architecture, data flow, and configuration options for PHI handling. What days work for you?

—
Marissa
Attachment: Redwood_BAA_Template.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-call: HIPAA / BAA eligibility & deployment options (MedWise)

Hi John — quick technical notes to help your security team map controls: 

1) Data flow: Inputs are accepted at the pinned endpoint. For Dedicated/Private we recommend disabling any cross-request caching for PHI endpoints (we can enforce via endpoint config). KV cache is per-deployment and not shared.
2) Encryption: TLS 1.2+/AES-256 at rest. Private offers customer-managed KMS; Dedicated offers Redwood-managed KMS by default (we can enable customer-managed KMS for Dedicated in some cases — will need contract language).
3) Logging/audit: request-level audit logs with request IDs, timestamps, and model version are available. Logs can be pushed to your S3, SIEM, or a Private Log Collector.
4) Data retention: configurable per-deployment. For PHI we recommend zero retention (reject storage of prompt/response beyond ephemeral processing) or strict retention with access controls.

I’ll prepare a short architecture diagram and a proposed config checklist for your security review before the call. Proposed times for a 30m call next week: Tue 28 Jul 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 29 Jul 14:00–15:00 PT. Let me know which works and I’ll send a calendar invite.
